subject: Finly \u0014 Discovery recap: p95 targets, streaming UX, concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finly.io>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@finly.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Finly  Discovery recap: p95 targets, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Thanks again for the time earlier today  great conversation. Per our call, below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we can align on scope for a PoC. Let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: user-facing latency spikes during streaming responses (search/assist flows). Customers drop out if the UI takes > ~1s to show the first partial response.
- Goal: improve perceived streaming UX (first-token latency) and guarantee p95 token latency targets under expected concurrency. Achieve predictable throughput for peak trading hours.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Frontend: React web app with streaming SSE consumer.
- Backend: Node.js microservice calling a hosted LLM endpoint (OpenAI at present) via a central API gateway.
- Observability: Datadog for app traces; limited token-level breakdowns today.

Success criteria (what Finly told us)
1) First-token streaming latency <= 400-500ms p95 for 95% of interactive sessions.
2) End-to-end p95 generation latency for medium requests (<= 512 tokens) < 1.5s under baseline concurrency.
3) Support sustained concurrency of ~200 concurrent streaming sessions with graceful degradation and fallbacks.
4) Instrumentation: token-level latency and cost per route to validate unit economics.

Key constraints
- Cannot route traffic through public proxies or third-party caching without SOC2 evidence.
- Encryption-at-rest + KMS for keys (enterprise requirement).

Immediate next steps / mutual action plan
1) Redwood: provide a short test plan (sample workload + synthetic trace) and a recommended benchmark script for streaming + non-streaming paths. (Deliverable: test-plan doc)
2) Finly: share a small anonymized sample trace and peak concurrency windows to size capacity. (Deliverable: traces + Datadog dashboard access if possible)
3) Redwood: provide an initial SLA draft + PoC proposal (capacity, metrics, timeline). We'll attach a draft SLA and a baseline pricing ballpark.
4) Align on dates: propose a 2-week PoC kick-off next week, 2-3 week execution window, then a measurement period.

Attachments: finly-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), SLA-draft-v1.docx (initial SLA + PoC outline).

If that looks right, I can schedule the kickoff and pull Aditya in to size the infra/instance types for the PoC.

Cheers,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finly.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@finly.io>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finly  Discovery recap: p95 targets, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Marissa - thanks for the super clear recap. This matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- First-token target: we actually want to aim for <= 350ms p95 if possible for high-value workflows (eg. live-investor-assist). The 400-500ms you called out is acceptable for lower-tier flows.
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent streaming sessions is our baseline for normal peak; during earnings we can spike to ~400 for ~30 minutes - would like to understand how Redwood handles short spikes and what the degradation profile looks like.
- Current model: we call OpenAI gpt-4o via a private integration today; exploring hosted/self-hosted options. We do some frontend-level batching (debounce), but no server-side k/v cache for prefixes.

Next items from our side: we'll share an anonymized 48-hour trace and approximate QPS pattern by EOD Monday. Also looping in Emily to coordinate security/review of the SLA draft.

Couple quick asks for the PoC proposal:
1) Can you include an expected instance/machine type and an estimated cost per 10k tokens for the proposed configuration?
2) Can you describe any streaming-specific optimizations Redwood applies (e.g., early-first-token kernels, prefetching KV, continuous batching) - high level is fine.

Thanks - Raj
VP Product | Finly
raj.patel@finly.io | (617) 555-0199
